headline: Bifurcation intensifying: premium brands and deep-discount platforms both winning simultaneously while middle-tier collapses.

deltas.reads: Premium identity brands (HOKA, UGG) with full-price selling capturing affluent consumers fleeing middle-tier
Off-price discovery model winning decisively as value-constrained consumers consolidate around lowest-cost platforms with branded bargains

deltas.change: traffic turned positive while comps held
deltas.reads: Consumables-heavy convenience platform winning on accessibility and low absolute price points; traffic recovery signals value consolidation
Middle-tier office equipment player losing share; lacks identity premium for price justification and lacks logistics scale to compete on cost

deltas.change: Bloomingdale's accelerating 1.4 points while core Macy's stalled
deltas.reads: Weak middle-tier Macy's comp contrasts sharply with luxury escape (Bloomingdale's +10%) showing clean split between identity premium and middle
Specialty retail middle tier losing customers; lacks both premium identity to justify full price and scale to compete on cost

deltas.change: positive comps despite weakening traffic; reliant on pricing architecture
deltas.reads: Lowest-cost platform consolidating value shoppers through multi-price mix; traffic decline signals middle-tier consumers captured upward or downward, not staying mid-market

momentum_note: The affordability ceiling is accelerating sharply. Deckers and luxury retail (Bloomingdale's +10% Q1 2026) capture affluent discretionary consolidation with full-price power, while Dollar General, Dollar Tree, and Burlington collectively show value-constrained consumers consolidating into low-cost platforms with strong traffic and comp acceleration. The middle tier (ACCO -8.5%, Macy's core +1.6%, Bath & Body Works -4.3%) is being hollowed out. This is not cyclical—it is structural sorting across categories simultaneously, visible in the same quarter across office equipment, specialty retail, footwear, and department stores.
